sections.html:
Ford County's seat sits on the Arkansas River in the southwest corner of the state, roughly 151 miles west of Wichita. People counted in 2020: 27,788. The July 2025 estimate: 27,653. The public schools belong to USD 443, which runs 14 buildings for over 6,000 students.

Beef is the town's industry. Cargill Meat Solutions and National Beef operate big plants, and a smaller crowd works at implement makers and the tourist attractions that trade on the Old West name. Ford County went from 24,315 residents in 1980 to 34,287 in 2020, driven by plant hiring, so plenty of the people shopping for a place to live work shifts at a packing house.

For a seller, that points to a mostly local buyer pool with many first-time owners. A tired house priced near move-in-ready homes will sit.

Summers are hot here and winters swing wildly. The thermometer tops 90 degrees on about 71 days a year and 100 degrees on about 14. Spring brings tornado season. Dodge City also has a reputation as the windiest town in the United States, averaging 13.9 mph.

All that wind is hard on shingles, fences and siding, which is exactly where a buyer's inspector starts. With storm damage on your house you can repair it before listing, list it with the damage disclosed and a lower price, or hand it over as is.

Floods in 1942 and 1965 brought federal flood control works along the Arkansas River, now mostly a dry bed. A dry bed says nothing about your lot. Pull the flood map for your parcel before you describe its risk to anyone.

sections.h2: How property valuation and tax billing work
sections.html:
The county handles it, not city hall. Ford County's appraiser discovers, lists and values every taxable and exempt parcel, real or personal, and answers at 620-227-4570. Billing comes from the Treasurer's tax department at 620-227-4536.

The Kansas calendar below applies to every county. If you disagree with a valuation notice, you file an equalization appeal within 30 days of the mailing date. Another route is paying under protest, which you file with the treasurer when you pay. Ford County gives December 20 as the date for that filing.

StepDate
Valuation notice mailedBy March 1
Equalization appeal window30 days from mailing
Informal meeting with the appraiserBy May 15
Hearing officer or panel hearingsWrapped up by July 1
Full payment or first halfDecember 20
Second halfMay 10

Before you list, ring the Treasurer and get the exact figure on your bill.

The tax lives with the parcel. A balance still open at your closing gets paid out of the sale proceeds by the title company, so past-due taxes do not stop a sale.

For the current year, Kansas has a default under K.S.A. 79-1805. A buyer takes on the year's tax for real property sold on or after January 1 and before November 1. A seller carries it for a sale made from November 1 to January 1. Contracts can override that, and most split the bill by days owned. Look for the split on your closing statement.

Kansas wants a Real Estate Sales Validation Questionnaire attached whenever a deed goes on record. Since every county runs its own register of deeds, ask the Ford County office how it takes the form. Most of the time the title company fills it out and files it along with the closing packet.

For work done to the house itself, Development Services and Inspections is the city department: planning and zoning, building inspections and code enforcement all sit there. The city's main line is 620-225-8100. An addition or deck built years ago may have no permit on file, and buyers or lenders sometimes ask, so find out before an offer arrives.

sections.h2: What do Dodge City sellers usually face?
sections.html:
A cash sale tends to appeal in a handful of situations:

  • Inherited houses. Heirs living in other states do not want to keep paying utilities and upkeep.
  • Out of area owners. Somebody has to handle showings, repairs and keys.
  • Tenants in place. A tenant limits when a buyer can inspect or move in.
  • Weather wear. A damaged roof can stall a buyer who needs a loan.
  • Unpaid tax. A delinquent balance has to be cleared from the proceeds.

Send us the Dodge City address if any of these fits, and we will walk through how a cash sale would play out for you.

sections.h2: What a cash sale skips and what it keeps
sections.html:
A listing costs time in places a cash sale does not touch: staging, open houses, a buyer's loan approval and the appraisal that goes with it. Here is what stays and what goes.

  • Stays: a title search, a deed, the questionnaire and a closing at a title company in Ford County.
  • Stays: payment of any unpaid tax or other balance from your proceeds.
  • Goes: repairs, cleaning out the last scuff mark, and weekend showings.
  • Yours: the closing date, including a later one if you need time to move out.

We look at the house as it stands and put a written offer in front of you. You can say yes, say no, or lay the offer beside a listing's costs in commission, repairs and months on the market.

Gather a few things before closing day: a photo ID, the keys and garage openers, any appliance manuals, and whatever you have on past roof or foundation work. If a buyer asks about a permit for an addition, tell them what you know and let the title company handle the rest.

Owners here usually choose among a listing with an agent, a sale by owner, and a cash offer. A listing can reach the most buyers but puts you through showings, inspection requests and the lender's schedule. A sale by owner saves a commission and hands you the marketing, the disclosures and the contract. A cash offer is quickest and most certain, and the price reflects the work the buyer takes on.

Whatever you pick, work out your own net. Subtract commission, repair bills, utilities while the house sits empty and the tax you will owe at closing from a listing price, then set the total beside the cash offer. The higher headline number is not always the higher check.

If a tenant lives in the house, read the lease first. The buyer steps into the landlord's place, so the lease terms, the deposit and the move-out date all matter. For an inherited house, the title has to be in the right names before a deed can be signed, and heirs who live out of state often need a notary where they are. Plan a little extra time for mailing papers back and forth. If you live far away, name one person in town who can meet the title company and hand over keys.

faqs.q: How many people live in Dodge City, Kansas?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 27,788 residents. The July 1, 2025 estimate is 27,653.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Dodge City?
faqs.a: Dodge City USD 443 covers the city with 14 schools and more than 6,000 students. Sacred Heart Cathedral School is a Catholic option.

faqs.q: Who handles property tax in Dodge City?
faqs.a: Ford County does. The appraiser sets the value and the county treasurer sends the bill. The first half is due December 20 and the second half May 10.

faqs.q: Is Dodge City prone to tornadoes?
faqs.a: Tornadoes and other severe storms are common here, especially in spring. Wind is a daily factor too, averaging 13.9 mph.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Dodge City house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer will look at the condition, make an offer and take the house as is. Tell the buyer about known problems such as roof damage.
